newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Saudi-Dutch storage joint venture to expand.
newsitem.headline: Saudi-Dutch storage joint venture to expand.

text.p: Dutch shipping and storage firm Koninklijke Pakhoed NV said on Wednesday its joint venture Sabic Terminal Services Company Ltd (SabTank) would expand its operations to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea.
Sabtank is a 75/25 joint-venture between Sabic Services, part of Saudi Basic Industries Corp, and Pakhoed unit Paktank Terminals BV.

SabTank was set up in 1995 to manage Sabic affiliates' liquid product handling and storage facilities at the King Fahd Industrial Port in Jubail. It will expand its services to Yanbu where two Sabic affiliates are raising their production.
Pakhoed said SabTank will be in charge of the construction supervision and the operation of the Yanbu facilities once they are completed.
Estimated project costs are $90 million, which includes the construction of a new berth and storage facilities.
Pakhoed said Paktank would assist in the design and construction supervision of the new facilities and in the setup of the Yanbu operation.
